report:
Not built: the cache on get_price conflicts with a recorded owner decision, so I stopped to ask first.

The conflict:
- docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-02: "No caching layer in the price service. Every call to get_price reads the live price." Reason: prices change every minute; a cached price once sold stock at last hour's price and caused a refund round. Decided by the owner.
- The request asks for a cache inside get_price. That breaks this decision directly.

What I found:
- basket_total calls get_price once per item. _fetch_live takes about 300 ms per call in production, so a basket of N items takes about N x 0.3 s, even when the same SKU appears many times.

Choices for the owner:
1. Keep the decision. Speed up basket_total without touching get_price: look up each distinct SKU once per basket_total call (live prices, nothing kept between calls). A basket with many repeats gets faster; a basket of all different SKUs does not.
2. Keep the decision. Fetch the distinct SKUs in parallel, or add a batch call to the pricing backend, inside basket_total. Still live prices.
3. Change the decision. Add a cache to get_price with a short expiry (for example under one minute). This reverses the 2026-09-02 decision and must be recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md by the owner.

No files changed. Tell me which choice to build.
